name: Neurosis
label: Alternative Tentacles
lede: In 1985 three Oakland punks decided their band would have keyboards and a slide projector. Four decades on, the records are still getting heavier.

eras.title: Three punks out of Violent Coercion
eras.text: Scott Kelly, Dave Edwardson and Jason Roeder start over in Oakland with Amebix records on the turntable and bigger plans than a hardcore band needs. The first album is fast, angry crust, and the ambitions wait their turn.

years.src: Wikipedia: Neurosis (band) · Noisecreep: Neurosis' Scott Kelly on Being a Father
years.h: Violent Coercion ends, and Neurosis takes its name from the intro tape
years.p: [[Scott Kelly|eb8277d5-0caf-467f-9d46-ed86059966bc]], [[Dave Edwardson|fefca00d-2b83-49a6-854a-4457f87a48f6]] and [[Jason Roeder|ec57f6b0-93ee-42c4-83b9-c3e42cfc81a2]] start over in Oakland. The new name comes from the intro track on a Violent Coercion tape.
years.xp:
The name came from "Neurosis/Faith or Fraud," the intro on a Violent Coercion tape, according to Wikipedia. The early sound drew on British crust, especially [[Amebix|612a476e-4d27-415f-b87c-a3a173284d4e]].

Kelly was 18 and the oldest of the three, he told Noisecreep, and the plan from day one was to add keyboards, extra instruments and visuals while staying independent.

years.cap: Flyer for a Neurosis show with Christ On Parade and Crimpshrine, Davis, California, October 9, 1987
years.src: Wikipedia: Pain of Mind · Wikipedia: Neurosis (band)
years.h: Pain of Mind crams fourteen songs into 37 minutes
years.p: Crust and crossover thrash on Alchemy Records, and the only Neurosis album with second guitarist [[Chad Salter|e25663c0-437b-4b6b-a159-9582d0a7cb7e]].
years.xp:
Salter joined in January 1987 and left in December 1988. Alchemy Records put the album out in December 1987.

The bonus disc on the 2000 reissue added live sets from Gilman Street and WFMU plus demo tapes, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: A second guitarist, then synths
eras.text: Steve Von Till takes the second guitar, a synth player and a projector arrive, and the songs stop fitting in three minutes. Lookout! puts out the records until Alternative Tentacles signs the band.

years.src: Wikipedia: Neurosis (band)
years.h: A roadie holds the second guitar until Von Till shows up
years.p: After Salter leaves in December 1988, roadie Pete Rypins plays second guitar until March 1989. Then [[Steve Von Till|97672881-2f1c-4aed-9cb7-a510ae9792dd]], ex-Transgressor and Peace Test, takes over.
years.xp: Rypins, a former roadie, played through a tour and left in March 1989, Wikipedia says. Von Till had also been in Tribe of Resistance.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Word as Law
years.h: Lookout! Records, the pop-punk label, puts out The Word as Law
years.p: The first Neurosis record with Von Till was recorded in December 1989 at Sound & Vision in San Francisco.
years.xp: The 1991 CD reissue added a cover of Joy Division's "Day of the Lords" and re-recorded older material from sessions on February 15-17, 1991, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Neurosis (band)
years.h: Keyboards and a projector arrive six years behind schedule
years.p: [[Simon McIlroy|f5b93e36-5b81-4ce0-94bb-a9fefe441974]] joins on synths and samples and Adam Kendall runs the visuals. It is the setup Kelly had wanted since 1985.
years.xp: Adam Kendall built the band's first live visual set, which he ran through 1997, according to Wikipedia. Pete Inc. took the projector after him, and [[Josh Graham|89849cea-2084-4de4-b596-3b8779d5705b]] followed in 2000 and made the art for three later albums before leaving in November 2012.

years.src: Wikipedia: Neurosis (band) · Brave Words: Scott Kelly Discusses Making Enemy Of The Sun
years.h: Jello Biafra's label signs Neurosis
years.p: Alternative Tentacles, home of the [[Dead Kennedys|37c78aeb-d196-42b5-b991-6afb4fc9bc2e]], becomes the band's next label after Lookout!.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the signing to October 1991. Scott Kelly told Brave Words that when the label first approached them, they "held them in high regard."

eras.title: Biafra at the board
eras.text: Two records for Alternative Tentacles turn a punk band into one with violins, a cello and a 26-minute song. Reviewers take a while to catch up.

years.cap: Neurosis in a promo photo for Souls at Zero, 1992
years.src: Wikipedia: Souls at Zero
years.h: Jello Biafra mixes Souls at Zero, and the violins move in
years.p: Recorded at Starlight Sound in Richmond, California, with Biafra as additional engineer and final mixer.
years.xp:
Kris Force played violin and viola, with a flutist, a cellist and a trumpeter also on the record. Wikipedia reports the first reaction as "mixed and confused," and AllMusic's Ned Raggett called it "too often too much of a good thing."

Decibel put it in its Hall of Fame in August 2016.

years.src: Wikipedia: Enemy of the Sun · Brave Words: Scott Kelly Discusses Making Enemy Of The Sun
yt: Enemy of the Sun, live New York 1995
years.h: Enemy of the Sun sets the template
years.p: Billy Anderson engineered and mixed. The original Cleanse runs 26:35; later reissues trim it to 15:54.
years.xp:
The cover is a statue at Toddington Manor in Gloucestershire, photographed by Simon Marsden, and the opening samples a scene from the film The Sheltering Sky.

Kelly was 25. He told Brave Words: "Every song and every moment on Enemy is deliberate."

eras.title: The record that defines them, then a week in Chicago
eras.text: Noah Landis takes the keyboards, Relapse Records puts out Through Silver in Blood, and the band turns down the major labels. Then it drives to Chicago and learns from Steve Albini that an album can be done in a week.

years.src: Wikipedia: Pain of Mind
years.h: Alternative Tentacles reissues Pain of Mind with R. Budd Dwyer on the cover
years.p: The 1994 vinyl reissue uses an image of the Pennsylvania politician tied to his 1987 televised suicide, and it causes controversy.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports the controversy but not who chose the artwork.

years.src: Wikipedia: Neurosis (band) · Wikipedia: Locust Star
years.h: Edwardson's childhood friend takes over the keyboards
years.p: [[Noah Landis|6f83d35d-6f44-4316-adfd-6439ea453253]] replaces McIlroy in early 1995 and completes the five-piece that stays together for 24 years. He and the band start Tribes of Neurot the same year.
years.xp: Tribes of Neurot is the band's ambient side project: same members, different rules. Its first record, Silver Blood Transmission, came out in 1995, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Rolling Stone: Neurosis on 30 Years · Wikipedia: Through Silver in Blood · Treble: Through Silver in Blood
years.h: Through Silver in Blood arrives on Relapse
years.p: Seventy-one minutes, tracked in December 1995 in Oakland with Billy Anderson, the band's first for Relapse. That is Von Till's phrase for making it.
years.xp:
Von Till used that phrase for the making of the album, in a Rolling Stone interview. Kelly said in the same piece: "I was addicted to everything. Never heroin, but I had a serious meth habit for a number of years." Wikipedia adds that Kelly was homeless at the time.

Rolling Stone later ranked it No. 49 on its 2017 list of the 100 greatest metal albums.

years.src: Wikipedia: Locust Star
years.h: A man crosses a wasteland in the Locust Star video
years.p: Neurosis and Andrei Rozen directed the clip, which came out on the Locust Star split EP with Tribes of Neurot.
years.xp: The EP, recorded 1994 to 1995 at Brilliant, Coast and Aurora House in Oakland, pairs four Neurosis tracks with three Tribes of Neurot pieces. Same five people on both halves.

years.src: Wikipedia: Neurosis (band)
years.h: Neurosis hits the road with Pantera
years.p: The band tours with Pantera in support of Through Silver in Blood.

years.src: Rolling Stone: Neurosis on 30 Years
years.h: Major labels want Neurosis; Neurosis wants an art film
years.p: After Through Silver in Blood, the majors came calling, and the band answered with a wish list.
years.xp: Von Till told Rolling Stone what the band's response was: "We gave them lists of bizarre shit that we wanted - like to make an art film and a book." The band stayed independent.

years.src: Wikipedia: Times of Grace (album) · Wikipedia: Fires Within Fires · MusicRadar: Steve Von Till on what Neurosis learned from Steve Albini
years.h: Neurosis books too much time for Times of Grace
years.p: Recorded in October and November 1998 at Electrical Audio in Chicago and Mr. Toad's in San Francisco, with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] producing for the first time.
years.xp:
The band contacted Albini in October 1998. Von Till told MusicRadar: "we booked way too much time, 'cos we were just used to all these techniques that wasted time." Albini showed them a whole album could be recorded and mixed in a week.

He went on to produce the band's records through Fires Within Fires in 2016.

years.src: Decibel: Grace Period · Wikipedia: Times of Grace (album)
years.h: Two stereos, two albums, one listener
years.p: Grace, from the side project Tribes of Neurot, is designed to run on a second player at the same time as Times of Grace.
years.xp:
The idea came from an experiment: "if you put two pieces of audio on at the same time, they do some very odd things," Edwardson told Decibel. The band pointed to the Flaming Lips' Zaireeka, which needs four discs.

The two records aren't time-synced. Von Till said the timing "had to be OK for it to be totally off but not conflict." Sound engineer Dave Clark's field recordings from San Francisco streets are on Grace. In 2009 both albums were packaged together as a 2xCD.

eras.title: Day jobs and a drive to Chicago
eras.text: Neurosis starts Neurot Recordings, keeps its day jobs and keeps going back to Albini's room. The records get quieter, then heavy again, then very heavy.

years.big: "The fewer people siphoning money out of the relationship."
years.src: Rolling Stone: Neurosis on 30 Years · Wikipedia: Neurot Recordings · Wikipedia: Neurosis discography
years.h: Neurot Recordings opens for business
years.p: That's Albini on the band's DIY label, per Rolling Stone, which dates Neurot to 2000. The Sovereign EP follows on October 31, 2000.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the label's founding to 1999 and the band's own page to the early 2000s; the first release is the safest anchor. Neurot became the home for Neurosis, Tribes of Neurot and later outside acts including Yob, Oxbow and OM.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Sun That Never Sets
years.h: A Sun That Never Sets slows down and sings
years.p: Albini recorded it at Electrical Audio. It brings clean vocals, acoustic guitars, folk textures and strings from Kris Force.
years.xp: The reviews split. AllMusic's Patrick Kennedy gave it 2.5 stars and said the band was "heading inexorably towards twilight." Decibel ranked it No. 18 among the decade's metal albums.

years.src: Wikipedia: Neurosis & Jarboe · Wikipedia: Neurosis discography
years.h: Jarboe of Swans writes the words for Neurosis & Jarboe
years.p: She wrote all the lyrics and the five members wrote all the music.
years.xp: Wikipedia gives conflicting release dates, October 21 and November 4, 2003. Terrorizer put it at No. 21 among its 2003 albums of the year. A remastered reissue with new art by [[Aaron Turner|db3ca919-a4ab-451a-8f03-e51310cfd866]] followed on August 2, 2019.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Eye of Every Storm
years.h: The Eye of Every Storm leans toward post-rock
years.p: Eight tracks, 68:52 and a slower burn, with Albini and Josh Graham both on it. Pitchfork gave it 7.0.

years.src: Wikipedia: Scott Kelly (musician)
years.h: Mastodon calls, and Kelly guests on six albums
years.p: His first Mastodon appearance is on Leviathan in 2004. He appears through 2017's Emperor of Sand.

years.cap: Scott Kelly and Steve Von Till at Hellfest, June 2007
years.src: Wikipedia: Given to the Rising · Roadburn: Deep Dives Neurosis 30th Anniversary
years.h: Albini produces Given to the Rising, and the band is heavy again
years.p: Albini also mastered it. Pitchfork's D. Shawn Bosler called it their best album in a decade.
years.xp: Graham's artwork drew on Budapest's Heroes' Square, an idea he and Von Till each came up with independently. Wikipedia lists release dates of both May 8 and June 5, 2007. The same year, Neurosis made its Roadburn debut.

years.src: Brave Words: Scott Kelly Discusses Making Enemy Of The Sun · Hellbound.ca: Scott Kelly of Neurosis · Punknews: Neurosis critical of Jello Biafra's Alternative Tentacles · Punknews: East Bay Ray releases statement
years.h: Neurot takes Enemy of the Sun back from Biafra's label
years.p: Kelly says Alternative Tentacles "cooked the books" over about $3,000. That is his account; the label's side isn't in the sources.
years.xp:
"Alternative Tentacles ripped us off. That's the simple version. They cooked the books and we called them on it," Kelly said in the Hellbound interview. Brave Words has him saying: "And it was only about $3000! It was basically an honor thing."

The 2010 reissue on Neurot was the first time the band owned the album, Kelly said. He said the aim was to "take the initial pressing back from Alternative Tentacles and stop the bleeding." I found no statement from Biafra or the label answering it. East Bay Ray of the Dead Kennedys later mentioned Neurosis in his own statement against Biafra.

years.cap: Neurosis at Tuska Open Air, Finland
years.src: Noisecreep: Neurosis' Scott Kelly on Being a Father
years.h: Von Till teaches third grade between tours
years.p: Around Honor Found in Decay, Kelly runs sound for a repertory theater and Edwardson supervises shipping at a warehouse.
years.xp: Noah Landis worked on sound design at a museum, per the Noisecreep interview. Kelly said: "I feel way more creative when I'm working a day job."

years.src: Wikipedia: Honor Found in Decay
years.h: Ten days at Electrical Audio for Honor Found in Decay
years.p: The whole band, keyboards included, played it live. The previous record got six days in the studio.

years.src: Roadburn: Deep Dives Neurosis 30th Anniversary
years.h: Roadburn hands Neurosis its main stage for the 30th anniversary
years.p: Two nights on the 013 main stage, April 16-17, 2016, plus a Von Till solo set.
years.xp:
Von Till said the band didn't enjoy looking backward but the venue and moment justified it. Roadburn's artistic director Walter called the shows "the epitome of everything that Roadburn was about."

There was also a Neurosis and Converge collaboration with [[Chelsea Wolfe|60e8e938-365e-4429-a141-4c79eb49588d]].

years.src: Wikipedia: Fires Within Fires
years.h: Kelly's last album with the band is five songs and 40 minutes
years.p: Albini recorded Fires Within Fires at Electrical Audio, starting December 27, 2015.
years.xp: Wikipedia notes CVLT Nation and Terrorizer ranked it their 2016 album of the year, and Rolling Stone ranked it No. 5 among the year's metal albums.

eras.title: Without the founder, then a surprise
eras.text: Neurosis parts with Scott Kelly in late 2019, and in 2022 he admits abusing his family. In 2024 the band starts rehearsing with Aaron Turner, and in March 2026 it puts out a twelfth album with no warning.

years.src: Stereogum: Neurosis Leader Scott Kelly · Consequence: Neurosis singer Scott Kelly · Wikipedia: Neurosis (band)
years.h: Scott Kelly admits abusing his family; the band says it cut him in 2019
years.p: On August 27 Kelly says on Facebook that he abused his wife and younger children and is retiring from music. Neurosis says it parted with him in late 2019.
years.xp:
Kelly described "emotional, financial, verbal and physical abuse," and wrote: "I am 100% permanently retired from being a professional musician," per Stereogum and Consequence.

The band said: "We cannot overstate the level of disgust and disappointment we feel for a man who we once called Brother." Wikipedia reports the band had stayed quiet earlier at his wife's request for privacy.

years.src: Wikipedia: Neurosis (band) · Bandcamp Daily: Inside the Miraculous Return of Neurosis
years.h: Aaron Turner of Isis and Sumac starts rehearsing with Neurosis
years.p: [[Aaron Turner|db3ca919-a4ab-451a-8f03-e51310cfd866]] joins first sessions in April 2024, though scheduling limits them.
years.xp: Von Till told Bandcamp Daily: "We wanted somebody to come up with new ideas and a fresh approach." Turner said songs get "chewed up by the Neurosis meat grinder."

years.src: Exclaim!: Steve Albini Dies at 61
years.h: Steve Albini dies of a heart attack at 61
years.p: He had produced Neurosis from Times of Grace in 1999 through Fires Within Fires in 2016.

years.cap: An Undying Love for a Burning World (2026).
years.src: Neurosis.com: Neurosis returns · Wikipedia: An Undying Love for a Burning World
yt: An Undying Love for a Burning World, full album
years.h: An Undying Love for a Burning World drops with no warning
years.p: Out March 20, 2026 on Neurot, it is the twelfth album and the first with Turner.
years.xp:
The band called it not a reunion because it "never broke up." It was recorded at Studio Litho in Seattle over three winter weekends and mixed in three days at Antisleep Audio in Oakland, according to the band's announcement.

Turner: "From the moment I first heard Neurosis over 30 years ago, I felt this was the music my heart and mind had been seeking."

years.src: Neurosis.com: Neurosis returns · Wikipedia: An Undying Love for a Burning World
years.h: First show in seven years, on Blackfeet Nation land in Montana
years.p: Neurosis headlines Fire in the Mountains, with Baroness, Enslaved, Yob and Agalloch on the bill.
years.xp: Von Till, on the board of the Firekeeper Alliance, called it "the most profound music event I have ever been a part of."
